pll1d16c1-d1e3477.summary: Turns to the Spirit's temporal procession, his mission or giving, distinct from his eternal procession from Father and Son, which is not from himself.
claims: The Spirit's eternal procession is not from himself.
The Spirit has a temporal procession, his mission or giving.

pll1d16c1-d1e3480.summary: Answers that, as the Son is sent in two ways, so the Spirit is sent or given in two ways by Father, Son, and himself: visibly, by a creaturely sign, as at Pentecost; and invisibly, daily entering the minds of the faithful.
claims: The Spirit is sent visibly and invisibly.
The Spirit was given visibly at Pentecost and other times.
The Spirit is given invisibly every day to the faithful.

pll1d16c1-d1e3483.summary: Proposes to treat first the visible mode of mission.

pll1d16c1-d1e3487.summary: With De Trinitate II: a creaturely form was made in time to show the Spirit, as the dove at Christ's baptism and the wind and tongues of fire at Pentecost. This visible work is called his mission, not because his invisible, unchangeable substance appeared, but so that hearts moved by the temporal sign would turn to the hidden Eternal. Lombard adds that the Spirit was not more in these creatures than in others, but in them for signifying; his coming was not by local motion, and the creature's motion signified his inner and invisible infusion.
claims: The visible mission was a creaturely form made in time.
The Spirit's substance remained invisible and unchangeable.
The sign served to turn hearts to the eternal.
The Spirit did not come by local motion.
The visible mission signified the invisible mission.

pll1d16c1-d1e3511.summary: Raises the question: since the Son is called less than the Father according to the mission in which he appeared in created form, why is the Spirit, who also appeared in created form, not called less?

pll1d16c1-d1e3514.summary: Shows from De Trinitate IV that the Son is less than the Father according to his mission: 'made of a woman' (Gal 4:4) means that he was sent in being made, and so is less insofar as made and made insofar as sent.
claims: The Son was sent in being made.
The Son is less than the Father insofar as made.

pll1d16c1-d1e3539.summary: Restates the question why the Spirit is not called less, since he too assumed a creature in which he appeared.

pll1d16c1-d1e3542.summary: Answers that the Spirit and the Son assumed creatures differently: the Son by union, becoming man, while the Spirit did not become a dove.
claims: The Son assumed humanity by union and became man.
The Spirit did not become a dove.

pll1d16c1-d1e3545.summary: Supports this with De Trinitate II: Scripture never calls the Father greater than the Spirit because the creature in which the Spirit appeared was not assumed as the Son of man was, in which the person of the Word was present not as having the Word but as being the Word. The Word in flesh differs from the Word made flesh. The Spirit did not beatify the dove, wind, or fire or join them to himself in unity of person forever.
claims: Scripture never calls the Spirit less than the Father.
The Word did not merely dwell in a man but became man.
The Spirit did not unite the dove or fire to himself in unity of person.
concepts: Verbum in carne vs Verbum caro

pll1d16c1-d1e3584.summary: Concludes that it has been shown in what respect the Son is less than the Father and why the Son, not the Spirit, is so called.
claims: The Son is less than the Father according to his humanity; the Spirit is not.

pl-l1d16c1.summary: Turns to the Spirit's temporal procession, which is his mission or giving. Like the Son, the Spirit is sent in two ways: visibly, in a creaturely sign (the dove, the wind and tongues of fire at Pentecost), and invisibly, by entering the minds of the faithful daily. With Augustine, the visible mission is a temporal sign made to turn hearts toward the hidden eternal one, not a manifestation of the Spirit's invisible substance; the Spirit did not move but signified his inner infusion. Asked why the Spirit is not called less than the Father, as the Son is according to his visible mission, Lombard answers that the Son assumed humanity into personal union, while the Spirit did not become a dove or unite the dove, wind, or fire to himself.
claims: The Spirit's temporal procession is his mission or giving, which is visible or invisible.
The visible mission was given through creaturely signs such as the dove and the tongues of fire.
In the visible mission the Spirit's substance was not seen; the signs pointed to his invisible infusion.
The Spirit did not move locally in coming; the creature's motion signified his spiritual infusion.
The Son is less than the Father insofar as he was sent, that is, made man.
The Spirit is not called less than the Father because he did not assume a creature into personal union.
